newsitem.title: Singapore: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in featureless trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. November consumer confidence index data, dealers said on Tuesday.
The consumer confidence index for November is forecast to rise to 109.0 percent compared with 106.2 percent reported in October.

"The market was quiet and featurless today and most people were sidelined due mainly to an absence of fresh incentives. Some people are waiting for tonight's release of the (U.S. November) consumer confidence index," a local dealer said.
"But unless the figures are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact here," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday, Wednesday/Thursday and week-fixed were unchanged from Monday's common 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent, respectively.
Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8, nine-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.
